html:
The collapse of the Oyo Empire, the largest Yoruba state, whose cavalry had dominated the savanna and the coast as far as Dahomey. It began with the revolt of its general Afonja at Ilorin in 1817 and ended with the abandonment of the capital, Oyo-Ile, in the 1830s.

Afonja allied with the Fula jihadists of the Sokoto jihad, and Ilorin became an emirate. Civil wars followed across Yorubaland, and new cities such as Ibadan and Abeokuta grew from war camps and refugees. Many captives of these wars were shipped to Brazil and Cuba, where their faith became Candomble and Santeria. Wars among Yoruba states lasted until the 1890s. See also the Yoruba.
